== Young Jedi names: page rule ==
Rule from Bill (25 October 2026): a person named only for Young Jedi gets a wiki page only if a source shows Star Wars CCG play. That can be tournament results, decklists, Retro League, GEMP, forum standings or similar. Without that, the name stays unlinked.

Checked 25 October 2026 against this wiki, the DeckTech report archive, Decipher's DecipherCon 2000 results pages and a web search:
* '''Philippe Parrise''' is [[Philippe Parise]]. Decipher's semifinal page also spells it "Parrise" ([https://web.archive.org/web/20020421134943/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/events/results/youngjedi3.html Young Jedi Finalists]). Dominic Gaudreault's Origins 2000 report calls Philippe Parise "the number 1 player in Ontario", which matches the article's Ontario, Canada. Player's Council titles the final video "Ian Vincent vs Philippe Parise".
* '''Avery Pollak''' is [[Avery Poliak]]. Decipher spells it "Avery Poliak". Tim Guzman's DCon 2000 Day 1 report says Avery Poliak "plays YJ" and "ended up a finalist in that". Dan Christy's Las Vegas report (March 2001) has Poliak playing Star Wars CCG.
* '''Ian Vincent''': Star Trek CCG at DecipherCon 1999 and FreedomCon 2001, Young Jedi champion in 2000. No Star Wars CCG play found. Unlinked.
* '''Jeremy Baker''': Young Jedi qualifiers at DecipherCon 1999 only. Unlinked.
* '''Jennifer Ekstrom''': the Young Jedi event at the 2000 Las Vegas Grand Slam (Chris Hines's report) only. Unlinked.
* '''Adam Fuentez''' and '''Irina Nepevna''': no other record found. Unlinked.
